nodes.name: Cu₂O film electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A two-electrode setup, which comprised of a mechanically polished copper disk as the working electrode and a platinum wire (99.99%, Sigma-Aldrich) as the counter electrode, was used. The Cu₂O film was galvanostatically deposited onto the copper substrate from a plating solution at −1.4 mA/cm² for 150 s. The plating solution consisted of aqueous 0.3 M CuSO₄·5H₂O (98.5-101%, GCE), 3.2 M NaOH (99%-100%, Chemicon) and 2.3 M lactic acid 85% (Sigma-Aldrich). A water bath was used to maintain the temperature of the electrochemical cell at 60°C.

nodes.name: Cu(OH)2 film anodization
nodes.procedure: The Cu(OH)2 film was prepared by anodizing a mechanically polished copper disk at a constant potential of 0.81 V for 15 min in 1 M KOH (99.99%, Sigma-Aldrich) electrolyte using a three-electrode setup. A platinum wire and a Hg/HgO electrode (1 M KOH, CHI 152, CH Instruments) were used as counter and reference electrodes, respectively.

nodes.name: CuO film electrodeposition on Cu
nodes.procedure: A two-electrode setup containing a platinum wire counter electrode was used. The CuO film was galvanostatically deposited from a plating solution at +5 mA/cm² onto a mechanically polished copper disk for 200 s. The plating solution contained aqueous 0.2 M CuSO₄·5H₂O and 0.2 M tartaric acid (99%, Alfa Aesar), which was adjusted to pH 13 using 4 M NaOH solution. The bath temperature was 30°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm pure phases: Cu metal, Cu₂O, Cu(OH)₂, and CuO for the respective as-prepared catalysts with no impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Only XRD patterns belonging to the underlying copper metal substrate and the electrodeposited film (CuO, Cu(OH)₂, or Cu₂O) were detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals Cu with abrasion markings, Cu₂O/Cu with pyramid-like structures, Cu(OH)₂/Cu with needle-shaped structures ~1-2 μm long, and CuO/Cu with particles <20 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphologies exhibited by the Cu₂O/Cu, Cu(OH)₂/Cu, and CuO/Cu samples consisted, respectively, of small pyramid-like structures, needle-shaped structures ~1-2 μm long, and particles <20 nm in size.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM surface area measurements mentioned but no specific surface area values or quantitative data reported for the catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surface area measurements of the electrodes were made using an atomic force microscopy (AFM) system... The measured currents were normalized against the surface areas of the catalysts, as determined using AFM (see section S4 in the Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: As-prepared Cu₂O shows Raman bands at 218/523/623 cm⁻¹, CuO at 298/347/591 cm⁻¹, Cu(OH)₂ at 490 cm⁻¹ with minor Cu₂O peaks at 523/623 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cu₂O and CuO films exhibited their characteristic Raman bands at 218/523/623 cm⁻¹ and 298/347/591 cm⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during CV shows all four catalysts form Cu₂O (523/623 cm⁻¹), then CuO (298/347 cm⁻¹) and Cu(OH)₂ (490 cm⁻¹), and CuIII oxide (603 cm⁻¹) at ≥1.62 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Above 1.62 V, where OER commences, a peak was observed at 603 cm⁻¹. This peak disappeared just outside the OER range at 1.55 V during the reverse cathodic sweep.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during chronoamperometry at 1.7 V shows Cu and Cu₂O/Cu form amorphous Cu oxide (594 cm⁻¹ broad band) without CuIII oxide, while CuO/Cu and Cu(OH)₂/Cu show sharp 603 cm⁻¹ CuIII oxide peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A sharp singlet peak at 603 cm⁻¹ was clearly detected on both samples, along with Raman peaks at 298, 347, and 490 cm⁻¹, which belong to CuO and Cu(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: NaCuO₂ standard shows characteristic Raman peak at 603 cm⁻¹ matching the CuIII oxide observed on catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum of NaCuO₂ displayed a strong, sharp peak at 603 cm⁻¹ with two other considerably weaker peaks at 500 and 1145 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Cu K-edge XANES of CuO/carbon cloth at 2.0 V shows ~0.3 eV blue shift indicating ~7% CuIII formation compared to CuO standard.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ CuO/carbon cloth K-edge shows a ~0.3 eV blue shift toward that of the NaCuO₂ standard. The shift in edge energy indicates an increase in the average valence of copper.
